content:
- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–30% for high sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for low sentiment periods.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., sentiment jumps to 1.00); apply a “cool-down” factor: reduce forecast by 20–40% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Forecasting horizon >14 days shows significant mean reversion bias; apply exponential decay to long-term forecasts (e.g., 0.85 decay per day after 14 days).
- If true outcome shows rapid decline after a high forecast, model may be lagging; adjust for 1–2 day lag in price drop; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for early correction.
- For sentiment history with alternating highs/lows, model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast mean with sentiment average over last 7 days.
